courses.title: Freedom and responsibility
courses.description: Six sessions in Jewish Thought: command, agency, tension, moral responsibility, and independent conceptual reading.

sessions.title: Hear the command to choose
sessions.prompt: What conceptual question does this command open?
choices: How command, human agency, and responsibility relate to each other.
How a disputed object is divided between two rival claimants.
At what hour the evening prayer obligation actually begins.
sessions.explanation: Jewish Thought begins with a source-grounded question — ‘choose life’ opens agency and responsibility, not a civil dispute or a timing rule.

sessions.title: Connect speech, heart, and action
sessions.translation: In your mouth and heart, to do it.
sessions.prompt: What relation does the verse establish?
choices: It joins speech, inward life, and action into one movement.
It separates words in the mouth from action in the world.
It sets out a historical timeline of when the Torah was given.
sessions.explanation: A conceptual claim should return to the precise terms of a source — mouth, heart, and doing are joined here, not separated or dated.

sessions.title: Name a tension
sessions.translation: Everything is foreseen, yet permission is given.
sessions.prompt: What is the careful first move?
choices: Hold both claims in view before forcing a resolution.
Resolve the tension by setting aside one half of the teaching.
Treat the tension as a copyist's error to be corrected.
sessions.explanation: Thought often starts by naming the exact claims a source holds together — foreknowledge and free will are both meant, not one to be dropped or fixed.

sessions.title: Distinguish topic and claim
sessions.prompt: Which is an argument rather than a topic label?
choices: Because choice is commanded, the verse frames agency as morally significant.
This passage is fundamentally about the subject of human freedom.
The source is an ancient and highly authoritative biblical text.
sessions.explanation: An argument links a claim to a source or reason — the others name a topic and cite authority, but neither reasons from the text.

sessions.title: Compare without flattening
choices: The shared question, and the precise claim on which the views differ.
Which of the two views is stated with the greater confidence.
The conclusion to reach before either source has been read closely.
sessions.explanation: Shared vocabulary can conceal a real conceptual disagreement — locate the shared question and the point of difference, not tone or a foregone conclusion.

sessions.title: Explain independently
choices: Define a term, state a claim, and explain how a source supports it.
Repeat the source's key word back without any explanation of it.
Set the source aside and offer a personal opinion in its place.
sessions.explanation: Independent reading is source-grounded explanation, not instant certainty — it defines and argues from the text, rather than echoing or abandoning it.

production.prompt: This command anchored the course. Type its English meaning from memory.
